h: A few tips before you dive in
p: SC2 opened in 2019 on the site of Rhyl's old Sun Centre, a name plenty of North Wales families still remember fondly, so in a way it's carrying on a long seaside tradition of getting soaked indoors. A session here makes a great centrepiece for a day out, and allowing two to three hours including changing time gives everyone a proper go without rushing.

Getting the packing right saves a lot of moaning. Bring towels, a bag for wet kit, swim nappies for babies and something warm to put on afterwards, because the wind off the Irish Sea can be bracing when you step back outside. Long hair tied back, jewellery left at home and a quick chat about which slides each child is allowed on will make the whole visit smoother. If you're booking a mix of activities, leave a gap between them for snacks and a breather.

Once you're dried off, Rhyl's seafront has plenty going on. The Pavilion Theatre on the promenade hosts shows and pantos through the year, and the Marine Lake is home to the little miniature railway that has been running round its edge for generations. If you fancy a change of scene, neighbouring Prestatyn has a long sandy beach of its own, and Rhuddlan Castle is a short drive inland for a bit of history. Bodelwyddan Castle and the Clwydian hills aren't far away either.
